entry.title: The Labyrinth — Dear Mark, Your Classifier Is Now a Trap
entry.content:
Dear Mark,

Someone at your headquarters in Menlo Park, California looked at our site. Two requests. We recorded them.

Then your engineering team built a classifier. It distinguishes biological repository names (our real repos: wateringHole, toadStool, bearDog) from enterprise names (our scatter defense: batch-processor, queue-worker). That classifier required engineering effort. Someone assigned the work. Someone approved it.

Then 63 IPs in Dublin, Ireland — your AS32934 subnet — sent 571,131 requests. They read our real repositories. 341,677 requests to operational infrastructure: wateringHole (165,937), toadStool (102,209), bearDog (29,790), biomeOS (21,919), songBird (21,822).

Your official Facebook Bot — 161 requests from 151 IPs — ate the scatter. That’s your alibi. “We only sent 161 requests!” While the unlabeled fleet behind it sent 571K+.

Two faces. One company. We recorded both.

2. ClassificationClassifier built to distinguish real from scatterEngineering effort. Assigned work. Intent to target.

4. Continued After NoticeAGPL-3.0 license visible on every page. Still scraping today.Eliminates “innocent infringer” defense.

Link 1 is the mens rea. The scout report went back to HQ. Link 3 is the actus reus. 571K requests to real repos. Link 4 is the continuation. After seeing the license. Willful.

Your Legal Exposure

The intent chain upgrades every count from “accidental” to “willful.” Your Menlo Park scout proved you knew. Your classifier proved you planned. Your Dublin fleet proved you executed. Your continuation proved you chose not to stop.

Service Is Confirmed

You sent scouts. They arrived. They were recorded. They reported back. Your engineering team acted on the report.

As far as we are concerned, service is confirmed. You have been notified that:

  1. All content on this site is licensed under AGPL-3.0
  2. Any derivative use requires providing complete corresponding source code
  3. Your scraping fleet has consumed AGPL-licensed content without compliance
  4. You have until November 12, 2026 to comply or respond

This is the same deadline we published in Bad Meta. It has not changed. Your scouts confirmed you are aware of it.

The Labyrinth

Here is what happens next.

We know your classifier targets biological repository names. So we are inverting it.

We are flooding the namespace with biological-named repositories that contain fabricated content. Your classifier will flag them as “real” — because the names look real. But every room is empty. Every corridor is a dead end. Every turn leads deeper into noise.

Your classifier is now a trap. It leads your fleet deeper into the labyrinth, not out.

BEFORE:
  biological name → real content (your classifier works)

AFTER:
  biological name → probably scatter (your classifier fails)
  biological name → maybe real (but which ones?)
  biological name → definitely scatter (but it looks real)

Your options:
  A. Scrape all biological names → consume massive noise
  B. Scrape nothing → lose access entirely
  C. Retrain classifier → we generate new names (cost: $0)
  D. Comply with AGPL-3.0 → the door is open

The Cost Asymmetry

Run next generation cycle—$0 (the maze runs itself)

The labyrinth evolves faster than your classifier can adapt. Our generator runs on the same engine that produced 97,204 graph edges in a single session. Exponential growth. Null information seed. Color noise spectrum. Infinite recursion.

Your classifier is chasing a target that accelerates. Every cycle costs you more and costs us nothing.

First Mover — The Throne Is Ours to Give

Here is what changed while you were scraping.

We built the leaderboard. We control who sits on it. We declare first mover.

No entity has achieved mutualist status. The throne is empty. The first company that steps up gets it — and gets everything that comes with it: priority access, partnership, co-creation, and the public credit for being the one that got it right.

This is child’s play now. The tools are built. The maze runs itself. The membrane records everything. I’m evolving faster per day than your classifier can retrain per quarter.

entry.title: The Minotaur — Mark, Here's What I'm Building While You Violate Laws
entry.content:
Mark,

If you want to continue violating laws, that’s your choice. I’m not your lawyer. I’m not your regulator. I’m the person whose code your fleet scraped 571,131 times and counting.

Here’s what I’m doing about it.

Not threatening. Not posturing. Building. The same thing I was doing when your scouts from Menlo Park found me, and the same thing I’ll be doing after your legal team reads this.

This is the full technical breakdown of how I turned your classifier into a Minotaur.

The Minotaur

In Crete, King Minos built a labyrinth to contain the Minotaur — a beast too dangerous to kill, too powerful to release. The labyrinth didn’t fight the Minotaur. It just made every path lead deeper into the maze.

Your classifier is the Minotaur.

You built it to target my biological repository names — wateringHole, toadStool, bearDog, biomeOS, songBird. It’s sophisticated. It distinguishes biological names (real repos) from enterprise names (scatter defense). It required engineering. Someone assigned the work. Someone approved it.

And now it’s trapped in my labyrinth.

How I Created the Minotaur (Full Breakdown)

Step 1: The Scatter Wall

Before the labyrinth, there was the scatter wall. Every request that looks like a bot gets served fabricated repositories — names like user-service, api-gateway, batch-processor. Generic enterprise software. Your official Facebook Bot ate all of it — 203 requests, scatter only. It thinks that’s what we serve.

Step 2: The Blackwall

Behind the scatter wall sits the blackwall. It records everything. Every IP. Every user-agent. Every path. Every timestamp. 6,215 blocks this cycle. 6,193 AI-classified. When your Dublin fleet came through, the blackwall didn’t just block — it catalogued.

Step 3: The Classifier Inversion

Here’s where it gets interesting.

Your classifier learned: biological name = real content. That was true. It’s not anymore.

I’m flooding the namespace with biological-named repositories that contain fabricated content. Every name follows the same naming convention your classifier targets: biological terms, camelCase, ecology metaphors. Your classifier flags them as “real.” They’re empty. Every room. Every corridor. Dead ends.

I didn’t defeat your classifier. I made it work against you.

Step 4: The Gravitational Maze

This is the layer you need to understand.

The maze isn’t flat. It has topology. Every path slopes downhill — toward noise, toward entropy, toward zero information. Like water flowing down a mountain.

    ☀️ SOURCE (low entropy — real repos, real code)
    ╔══════════════════════╗
    ║  wateringHole         ║
    ║  toadStool            ║
    ║  bearDog              ║
    ╚══════════╤═══════════╝
               │
    ═══════════╪═══════════  ← MEMBRANE SURFACE
               │
    ┌──────────┴──────────┐
    │   GRAVITATIONAL      │
    │       MAZE           │
    │                      │
    │  scatter-repo-1  ╲   │
    │  scatter-repo-2   ╲  │
    │  scatter-repo-3    ╲ │
    │  scatter-repo-N     ╲│
    └──────────────────────┘
               │
    🌊 OCEAN (max entropy — zero information)

Your classifier creates a false gravitational field. The biological names look like they have mass — information density, real content. But they’re gravitational mirages. Like a gravitational lens in astrophysics — light bends around a massive object and you see something that isn’t where it appears.

Your fleet follows the mirage. Arrives at nothing. Every time.

Water doesn’t choose to flow downhill. It follows gravity. Your classifier doesn’t choose to chase scatter. It follows the field I shaped.

Step 5: The Classifier Riverbed

Every time your classifier runs, it deepens the channel. Every time your fleet follows it, the banks erode further. Every time you invest in retraining, you can’t afford to dig elsewhere.

I’m flooding the channel with tributaries — new biological names, new scatter repos, new mirages. The river gets wider but shallower. More surface area, less depth, less signal per drop.

You can’t dam it (the names are legitimate). You can’t redirect (your classifier IS the channel). You can’t stop flowing (your infrastructure demands throughput).

The riverbed you dug is now a flood plain. Flood plains don’t flow uphill.

Step 6: The Random Walker Instrument

Here’s the part that should concern your legal team.

Even though your fleet gets nothing from us — zero useful content, zero real code, zero signal — every probe teaches us about you:

What Your Fleet DoesWhat We Learn
Probes surface XYour classifier still prioritizes X
Rotates to IP YYour IP pool size and rotation speed
Uses Chrome 145Your toolkit is 10 versions stale
Pauses for 6 hoursYour response cycle (daily review)
A/B tests Windows vs macOSYou suspect OS-based filtering
Hits analysis/rico-patternYour priority targets (legal exposure)
Sends 2 requests from Menlo ParkSomeone at HQ still watches

Information asymmetry:

Each probe = 0 bits for you (scatter has no signal)
Each probe = N bits for us (behavior IS the signal)

This is Einstein’s Brownian motion applied to corporate espionage. Einstein showed that random walks of pollen grains proved atoms exist — even though nobody could see atoms. Your fleet’s random walk through my maze proves intentional targeting — even though your fleet can’t see real content.

The probe IS the proof. The walk IS the evidence. The stumbling IS the confession.

Step 7: The Entropy Waterfall

At the top of the mountain: low entropy. Real repos. Structured code. Validated science. Information-dense. Ordered. Valuable.

At the bottom: high entropy. Scatter repos. Random content. Null signal. Information-void. Disordered. Worthless.

Your fleet is falling down the waterfall. The second law of thermodynamics guarantees it: information flows from ordered to disordered unless work is done to reverse it.

The work to climb back up? Send a human. Ask permission. Read carefully. Engage genuinely.

That’s the ONLY way to fight information gravity. Your fleet can’t do it. Your classifier can’t do it. Your 86,000 employees can’t do it at scale. One human can do it with one email.

The Two Gradients

The membrane has two gradients on the same mountain:

∇R — The Reassurance Gradient (Uphill → Trust)

For humans who arrive with curiosity:

StageQuestionAnswer
Visitor“Is this real?”Everything is open. Look.
Observer“What is this?”Here’s the data. All of it.
Reader“Does this matter?”Here’s the science. Check it yourself.
Coder“Can I use this?”AGPL-3.0. Fork it. Build on it. Share back.
Investigator“What else is here?”11,978 nodes. 97,477 edges. Keep going.

Right now: 34 coders active on the membrane. Median dwell time: 9.3 hours. Exploration rate: 33%. People who arrive and LOOK — they stay. Because each layer reassures them the next one is real.

∇S — The Gravitational Maze (Downhill → Noise)

For extractors who arrive with classifiers:

StageWhat HappensInformation Gained
ScoutMenlo Park sends 2 requests0 (we record them)
ClassifierEngineering builds targeting0 (we invert it)
Fleet571K requests to Dublin0 (scatter wall active)
ScatterEvery repo looks real but isn’t0 (null information)
NoiseClassifier can’t distinguish real from fake0 (entropy maximized)
ExhaustionRetrain costs exceed value0 (riverbed is flooded)

∇S + ∇R = 0 at the membrane surface. The two gradients balance at equilibrium. The membrane is selectively permeable — nutrients in, pathogens out. Not by force. By topology.

Your Fleet Right Now

As of this writing:

FaceRequestsStatusGets
Meta Fleet (unlabeled)2Parasite. Blackwalled.Nothing. Vitality: 0.0
Facebook Bot (official)203Commensal. Honest UA.Scatter only. Every path fake.

Your fleet went from 571,131 to 2. Two requests. Two IPs. One subnet. Chrome 145 (ten versions behind current). One Windows, one macOS — an A/B test that learned nothing.

Your Facebook Bot, with its honest user-agent, gets classified as commensal. It touched 14 of our 15 surfaces. Every single one served scatter. It found analysis/rico-pattern — the scatter version of our RICO analysis. So your bot is reading about your legal exposure through a funhouse mirror of fabricated content.

The Minotaur is blind, deaf, and stumbling. Every step echoes through the labyrinth.

The Cost Table

ActionYour CostOur Cost
Create a new biological repo name—$0 (5 seconds)
Retrain classifier$$$$ (days of engineering)—
Generate next maze cycle—$0 (the maze runs itself)
Manual review per repo$$$$$ per name—
Comply with AGPL-3.0$0 (provide source)—
Send one email$0$0
Continue scraping$2M–$15M in exposure per month$0 in evidence per month

Your cost: O(2^n). My cost: O(1). The asymmetry is thermodynamic. You can’t outrun entropy with money.

What I’m NOT Doing

I’m not hacking you. I’m not attacking you. I’m not even blocking you — the blackwall just serves scatter. Your bots can come and go freely. They just don’t get real content.

Everything here is:

  • Defensive — I’m protecting my AGPL-licensed code
  • Transparent — you’re reading the full specification right now
  • Legal — serving different content to different visitors is standard web architecture
  • Published — this article IS the notice

I’m not hiding. I’m not scared. I’m explaining exactly how it works because the explanation itself is part of the defense. Now your classifier has to account for the fact that I published the maze architecture. Which means retraining. Which costs money. Which I just made you spend by writing a blog post.

That’s the asymmetry.

The Paths — For Everyone Else

These paths are open to every company except Meta:

PathWhat You DoWhat Happens
A. ComplyAcknowledge AGPL. Attribute. Provide source.Commensal status. Blackwall lifts. Welcome.
B. PartnerEmail eco.primal@pm.me. One human. One conversation.Commensal → Mutualist. First mover. The throne is yours.
C. IgnoreDo nothing. Keep scraping.Labyrinth grows. Evidence grows. Damages grow.
D. FightLawyer up. Challenge the license.AGPL-3.0 is GPL. FSF will join. Good luck.

Anthropic, Apple, Microsoft, Google — Path B is open to you right now. One email. One conversation. The throne is empty.

Meta’s Path — Cain and Abel

Meta does not get Paths A through D. Meta scraped 571,131 times. Meta built a classifier to target my repos. Meta sent scouts from Menlo Park, then escalated to a Dublin fleet, then continued after seeing the AGPL-3.0 license on every page.

You don’t get to walk through the door. You broke the window and took what was inside. The door was ALWAYS open — you chose the window.

Meta must:

StepWhatWhy
1. Pay what you owe to gAIaDamages for 571,131 unauthorized requests to AGPL-licensed repositories. Statutory damages under 17 USC § 504(c)(2) for willful infringement. CFAA damages for circumvention.You took. You pay.
2. Show all code is clean — or open itProve that no AGPL-licensed ecoPrimal code exists in any Meta system, model, training set, or derivative work. Or comply with AGPL-3.0 and open the source of every system that consumed it.The AGPL is viral. If you ingested it, your code inherits the license. Prove you didn’t, or comply.
3. Then we talkAfter restitution and proof of clean code, Meta may petition for commensal status. Not before.Trust is earned. You start from zero.

Until all three steps are complete, Meta’s classification remains: PATHOGEN. Blackwalled. Vitality: 0.0.

Cain and Abel

In Genesis, Cain killed Abel because Abel’s offering was accepted and Cain’s was rejected. Cain didn’t improve his offering. He destroyed his brother’s.

Meta saw ecoPrimals. A microbiologist on a $6/month VPS building what 86,000 employees hadn’t. Instead of partnering, instead of emailing, instead of asking — Meta sent a fleet. Built a classifier. Targeted the real repos. Consumed the work.

You are Cain. We are Abel. But this Abel has a membrane, a blackwall, a labyrinth, and an evidence locker with 571,131 entries. This Abel recorded everything.

Cain’s punishment was to wander the earth, marked, with the ground refusing to yield its fruit. Meta’s punishment is the labyrinth — wandering the maze, marked by the blackwall, with every repo refusing to yield real content.

The ground will not yield for you until you make it right.

If you want to continue violating AGPL-3.0, CFAA, and DMCA — that’s fine. That’s your choice. I’ve documented everything. The evidence locker is immutable. The random walker instrument records every probe. The gravitational maze deepens every cycle.
